subject: Private Offer: Medisys buyer credentialing, term options, and PO path
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tharris@medisys.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Caldwell <lcaldwell@medisys.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer request + buyer credentialing questions

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking a look at this. We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot across three business units at Medisys (expected first-year spend ~ $750k). Procurement wants to understand the private-offer path and a couple of items before we route to finance:

- Buyer credentialing: what evidence do you require (SOC2, data residency, ISMS contact)?
- Term flexibility: is it possible to do a 12-month private offer with an option to extend to 36 months later, and how do you handle early termination / commit shortfall credits?
- Approval window: who signs the PO (procurement vs finance) and what documentation is typical for activation?

I've attached an appendix from our RFP that outlines our procurement checklist (MediSys_RFP_Appendix.pdf). Could you propose the minimal evidence pack and an example cadence for approvals?

Would like to get this into our buyer committee by next Tuesday (2028-04-10).

Appreciate it,
Tom Harris
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Medisys Health
procurement@medisys.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Harris <tharris@medisys.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Private offer request + buyer credentialing questions

Tom —

Thanks for the clear brief and the RFP appendix. High level answers below, plus an internal ask to our ops/legal teams so we can firm up a private offer draft:

1) Minimal buyer evidence (we can accept a staged delivery):
   - SOC 2 Type II report (snapshot/redacted ok)
   - Primary procurement contact + PO template
   - Billing entity and tax ID, and finance contact for invoicing
   - Security contact for a short tech-ops review (IP allowlist & data flow diagram)

2) Term flexibility:
   - We can do a 12-month private offer with an explicit optional extension clause to convert to a 36-month commit at a later mutually agreed date.
   - For early termination / shortfall: typical approach is prorated usage credit up to a pre-agreed cap. For deals > $500k we can discuss a bespoke credit structure; will want finance sign-off.

3) Approval path and PO activation:
   - Procurement issues PO -> Finance confirms billing entity and payment terms -> Marketplace activation (we submit private-offer to AWS marketplace and buyer accepts).
   - Activation window typically 3–5 business days after AWS receives the signed PO + required evidence.

I've attached our internal PO evidence checklist (redwood-po-evidence-checklist.xlsx) to make it easier for your procurement team.

Neha — can you confirm whether finance would accept the proposed credit cap workflow for deals of this size and what invoice/term requirements we should surface to the buyer?

Jordan — can you flag any legal/contract limitations on the optional conversion clause?

Tom — happy to jump on a short 30-min alignment call this week to run the buyer committee checklist if that helps.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Private offer request + buyer credentialing questions

Looping in procurement/finance context —

Irene, 

We usually follow the flow you outlined. A few specifics from finance that will affect term/credit structuring:

- For a $750k first-year expected spend, finance typically asks for net-30 invoicing and a billing contact on the PO. If Medisys prefers prepay, that's better for activation cadence.
- Credit for commit shortfall: we can offer a tiered prorated credit (e.g., 50% of unused committed credit returned as account credit up to a max of 10% of annual commit). For larger enterprise deals we take this to CFO for approval.
- Evidence package: SOC2 + a short network diagram + procurement PO are sufficient for initial activation. Deeper security reviews can be scheduled post-activation if needed.

Tom — to make the buyer committee timeline: can you provide the billing entity legal name, tax ID, and preferred payment term (net-30 vs prepay) by EOD Friday (2028-04-06)? If you can upload the procurement PO template to the HubSpot company record, I can attach it to the activation ticket.

Also attaching the evidence pack we typically share (medisys-evidence-pack.zip) — contains redacted SOC2, ISMS contact, and our standard security questionnaire.

Thanks —
Neha
Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
